title.value: Systematic Evaluation of Causal Discovery in Visual Model Based Reinforcement Learning
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the paper.
title.quote: Systematic Evaluation of Causal Discovery in Visual Model Based Reinforcement Learning

analysis.description: The paper evaluates the ability of model-based reinforcement learning methods to discover and use high-level causal relationships from low-level inputs. It proposes new RL environments specifically designed to study causal induction and systematically assess various models' capacity to capture causal structures in these environments. The suit of environments allows for evaluating models with explicit structure and modularity, specifically in the context of deep reinforcement learning.

type.justification: The paper includes experiments and evaluations of models in newly proposed RL environments designed to study causal induction.
type.quote: Our experiments seek to answer the following questions... We report the performance of our models on both the Physics and the Chemistry environments, and refer the readers to Appendix F for implementation details.

name.justification: The paper focuses on model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) for studying causal induction.
name.quote: Deep learning methods have made immense progress on many reinforcement learning (RL) tasks in recent years.

name.justification: The paper extensively discusses causal induction and the discovery of causal structures within the context of reinforcement learning.
name.quote: Inducing causal relationships from observations is a classic problem in machine learning... A central goal for AI and causality is thus the joint discovery of abstract representations and causal structure.

name.justification: The paper evaluates various representation learning algorithms from the literature to find effective means of causal induction.
name.quote: We evaluate various representation learning algorithms from the literature and find that explicitly incorporating structure and modularity in models can help causal induction in model-based reinforcement learning.

name.justification: The paper discusses the use of Graph Neural Networks as models for causal induction in MBRL.
name.quote: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have a factorized representation of variables and can model undirected relationships between variables.

is_contributed.justification: The paper uses GNNs but does not introduce them as a new model contribution.
is_contributed.quote: We evaluated two typical monolithic models (autoencoders and variational autoencoders) and two typical models with explicit structure: graph neural networks (GNNs) and modular models.

is_executed.justification: The paper does not provide details on executing GNNs on specific hardware like GPU or CPU.
is_executed.quote: We evaluate various representation learning algorithms... and measure progress.

is_compared.justification: GNNs are compared against other models for their ability to perform causal induction.
is_compared.quote: This suggests that explicit structure and modularity such as factorized representations and directed edges between variables help with causal induction in MBRL.

referenced_paper_title.quote: In particular, we consider the C-SWM model [Kipf et al., 2019], which is a state-of-art GNN used for modeling object interactions.

name.justification: Modular models with explicit structures are used and evaluated for causal learning.
name.quote: Modular networks also have a factorized representation of variables, along with directed edges between variables which can model directed relationship such as A causing B.

is_contributed.justification: The paper contributes novel insights and implementations of modular networks for causal learning in MBRL.
is_contributed.quote: We found that even our naive implementation of modular networks can scale significantly better compared to other models.

is_executed.justification: The execution details of models on specific hardware like GPU or CPU are not provided.
is_executed.quote: We evaluate various representation learning algorithms... and measure progress.

is_compared.justification: Modular models are compared with other models in terms of causal induction efficiency.
is_compared.quote: Modular models also have a factorized representation of variables, along with directed edges between variables...

referenced_paper_title.justification: The modular network approach is connected to previous work on neural causal models.

name.justification: Varieties of autoencoders are used as baseline models for performance comparison.
name.quote: We evaluate causal induction on two commonly used monolithic models: multilayered autoencoders and variational autoencoders.

is_contributed.justification: These models are existing baseline models and not new contributions in the paper.

is_compared.justification: These models are used as benchmarks for comparison against more structured models like GNNs and modular models.
is_compared.quote: The GNN and Modular models trained on constrastive loss significantly outperform the monolithic models (autoencoders and VAE).
